items.title: Germany Secures Direct 50% Stake in KNDS
items.summary: The German federal government reached a final agreement with the Wegmann-Holding owner families to directly take over their 50% private stake in KNDS.

sections.label: What happened
lines: The German federal government reached a final agreement with the Wegmann-Holding owner families to directly take over their 50% private stake in KNDS.

sections.label: Context
lines: 15 Dec 2015: Krauss-Maffei Wegmann (KMW) and Nexter Systems complete their formal merger to create the joint holding company KNDS (KMW + Nexter Defense Systems), headquartered in Amsterdam, structured as a 50/50 arrangement between the French state and the German founding families.
19 Feb 2025: KNDS hires financial advisers to explore a potential initial public offering (IPO) on public markets as early as late 2025 or 2026.
15 Sep 2025: KNDS management is instructed by the board to prepare for a public stock market listing, while discussions continue regarding a potential anchoring stake by the German government.

24 Jun 2026: The Bundestag's Budget Committee approves an initial ceiling of up to €7.2 billion for the federal state (acting through KfW) to acquire a 40% stake in KNDS linked to the planned IPO (Approved, EUR 7.2 billion).
Jul 2026: The planned dual-listing (IPO) of KNDS in Paris and Frankfurt is formally suspended due to unfavorable market valuations and investor resistance against valuation targets of ~€15 billion.
14 Oct 2026: Negotiations pivot toward a direct state purchase of the entire 50% German family-owned stake after institutional investors decline to meet valuation expectations.
5 Nov 2026: The German government and the Wegmann-Holding owner families reach a final agreement for the federal state to take over the 50% private stake directly (Agreement).

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: EU — White Paper for European Defence – Readiness 2030 and ReArm Europe Plan (2025-03-19): Close critical capability gaps in seven priority areas (including air and missile defence and artillery) and build a stronger European defence industrial base; ReArm Europe enables over €800 billion of defence spending.

EU — Council Regulation establishing the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) instrument (2025-05-27): Up to €150 billion in EU loans for member states investing in defence industrial production through common procurement of priority capabilities.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: After a planned IPO was suspended on 1 July 2026 due to unfavorable market valuations, negotiations pivoted on 14 October 2026 toward a direct state purchase, resulting in the final agreement on 5 November 2026 to secure state ownership alongside the French state.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: KNDS Deutschland depends on RENK Group AG.
Germany: export licensing on Military land system transfers to third countries (in_force).

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Defence procurement and supply chain professionals should monitor how direct federal ownership of KNDS Deutschland impacts land system export licensing and national industrial integration.

items.title: SNC drops UJTS bid over fixed-price risks
items.summary: Sierra Nevada Corporation confirmed it will not submit a bid for the Undergraduate Jet Training System due to the Navy's insistence on firm-fixed-price production before design maturity.

Defense Minister Boris Pistorius announced the selection, highlighting Freuding's experience overseeing arms supplies to Ukraine and modernizing land forces.

12 Apr 2026: Fincantieri Marinette Marine secured an initial contract for early long-lead material procurement and production preparation (Contract).

items.title: ST Engineering Debuts MRV Mothership Concept at Euronaval 2026
items.summary: ST Engineering debuted its Multi-Role Vessel unmanned-systems mothership concept at Euronaval 2026 in Paris. The 150-metre platform is designed to deploy and coordinate offboard unmanned systems while maintaining independent air defence and surface capabilities.

lines: Mar 2018: The Republic of Singapore Navy and DSTA publicly outlined initial concepts for a new Multi-Role Combat Vessel (MRCV) class to replace aging missile corvettes.
Mar 2023: Singapore's Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) awarded ST Engineering the detailed design and construction contract for a fleet of six MRCVs (Contract).
22 Oct 2024: ST Engineering held the official keel-laying ceremony for the first-of-class MRCV (Victory) at its Benoi Yard.
21 Oct 2025: ST Engineering launched the lead ship, Victory, at its Benoi Yard in Singapore.
23 Jul 2026: ST Engineering launched the second MRCV, Valour.
3 Sep 2026: ST Engineering conducted the keel-laying ceremony for the third MRCV hull.
5 Nov 2026: ST Engineering showcased its MRV export concept making its European debut at Euronaval 2026 in Paris.

items.title: France weighs future in European Patrol Corvette amid industrial shifts
items.summary: Uncertainty surrounds France's continued commitment to the European Patrol Corvette project initiated in 2019.

sections.label: What happened
lines: Uncertainty surrounds France's continued commitment to the European Patrol Corvette project initiated in 2019.

sections.label: Context
lines: Jun 2019: Italy and France sign a Letter of Intent to initiate a collaborative naval project for future patrol corvettes.
12 Nov 2019: The European Council formally adopts the European Patrol Corvette (EPC) as a Permanent Structured Cooperation (PESCO) project.
Jul 2021: The European Commission awards the initial concept and design proposal submitted by the Naviris-led consortium (Contract, EUR 87 million).
Dec 2021: The European Commission and OCCAR sign a Contribution Agreement entrusting OCCAR with management of the EPC preparation phase (Agreement).
24 Oct 2023: OCCAR signs the Modular and Multirole Patrol Corvette (MMPC) Call 1 contract worth €87 million with the Naviris consortium for the first phase of design (Contract, EUR 87 million).
26 Feb 2026: Navantia and Fincantieri sign a Memorandum of Understanding to establish a joint venture to coordinate and execute the EPC project development and commercialisation (Agreement).

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: The European Patrol Corvette has evolved from a 2019 collaborative plan into a structured PESCO framework managed by OCCAR, moving toward consolidated joint ventures for development and commercialisation.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: EPC Programme depends on CODLAD / CODAD marine propulsion diesel engines and reduction gearboxes.

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Naval supply chain managers and prime contractors should monitor shifting national commitments and joint venture formations affecting propulsion and subsystem procurement.

items.summary: Organizers announced the permanent relocation of the Royal International Air Tattoo from RAF Fairford to MOD Boscombe Down following operational uncertainties and the cancellation of the 2026 air show.

items.title: USMC and Navy Finalize Requirement for 40 Amphibious Ships
items.summary: Senior Marine Corps officials confirmed that joint analysis finalized a requirement for 40 amphibious ships, consisting of 13 big-decks and 27 LPDs, to maintain a 3.0 ARG/MEU posture.

sections.label: What happened
lines: Senior Marine Corps officials confirmed that joint analysis finalized a requirement for 40 amphibious ships, consisting of 13 big-decks and 27 LPDs, to maintain a 3.0 ARG/MEU posture.

sections.label: Context
lines: Jun 2000: Construction of the lead ship of the San Antonio-class (LPD 17) formally began at Avondale Shipyard.
2022: The Marine Corps formally articulated a minimum operational floor of 31 amphibious warfare ships under updated force planning guidance.

3 Dec 2024: The Government Accountability Office (GAO) published report GAO-25-106728 highlighting that maintenance delays and poor material readiness severely constrained the operational availability of the 31-ship amphibious fleet.
Sep 2025: The Department of the Navy awarded a Multi-Ship Procurement (MSP) contract covering LHA 10 and LPDs 33–35 (Contract).

23 Apr 2026: Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Eric Smith announced at the Sea-Air-Space conference that the 31-ship statutory minimum is insufficient to meet global combatant command requirements for 3.0 ARG/MEU presence.

19 May 2026: Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao endorsed a joint Navy-Marine Corps proposal originating from the Amphibious Force Readiness Board (AFRB) to expand the objective fleet size to 40 amphibious warfare ships.

5 Nov 2026: Senior Marine Corps officials confirmed that joint analysis between the Navy and USMC finalized the concrete requirement for 40 amphibious ships (13 big-decks and 27 LPDs) to permanently maintain a 3.0 ARG/MEU deployment posture.

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: US — NSPM: Rebuilding the United States Navy and America's Shipbuilding Industrial Base (2026-08-13): Fix long-term problems in Navy shipbuilding and repair: a fifth Naval shipyard, a submarine Component Repair Center, reorganisation of NAVSEA and direct investment in shipyards on the 'Finland model'.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Following the 2022 establishment of a 31-ship operational floor and subsequent 2024 GAO readiness warnings, the Navy and Marine Corps advanced from a 2026 proposal to a finalized 40-ship objective in November 2026, signaling increased demand for naval constructors.

lines: Shipbuilding prime contractors and propulsion suppliers should prepare for potential long-term capacity expansions tied to the newly expanded 40-ship fleet objective.

items.summary: Rheinmetall revised its 2026 sales outlook to roughly €13.2 billion and its operating margin to approximately 18.5% due to administrative deferrals in the Arminius project and delayed artillery ammunition lot acceptances.

lines: Rheinmetall revised its 2026 sales outlook to roughly €13.2 billion and its operating margin to approximately 18.5% due to administrative deferrals in the Arminius project and delayed artillery ammunition lot acceptances.

sections.label: Context
lines: 19 Dec 2025: Rheinmetall announces major production expansions and order activities for the Boxer platform family and related weapon systems.
8 May 2026: Rheinmetall CEO Armin Papperger outlines the prospective Arminius umbrella framework valued up to €40 billion, indicating contracting shifts between BAAINBw and OCCAR.

6 Aug 2026: CEO Papperger specifies that Arminius entails a framework of up to €75 billion total potential value, with a firm initial order share for Rheinmetall valued at roughly €12.4 billion slated for late 2026.
29 Oct 2026: Germany and the Netherlands utilize OCCAR to order 69 additional Schakal/Boxer variants under existing options, reinforcing production pipelines ahead of the broader programme.

2 Nov 2026: Industry reports leak that the core Arminius firm procurement contract faces administrative deferral to February 2027, trimming roughly 10% of auxiliary service costs while preserving vehicle volume targets (Contract).

5 Nov 2026: Rheinmetall officially cuts its full-year 2026 sales forecast to €13.2 billion and operating margin to ~18.5%, citing the Arminius contract slip and delayed artillery ammunition lot acceptances.

lines: While capacity expansions in the UK, Spain, and Germany support long-term growth across vehicle and air defence platforms, short-term contract slips like the Arminius deferral highlight near-term schedule friction.

items.title: General Atomics Unveils Air-Launched Vektrex Missile Concept
items.summary: General Atomics debuted a conceptual graphic at Euronaval 2026 showing an F/A-18E/F Super Hornet launching a missile loaded with seven Vektrex maneuvering projectiles.

sections.label: What happened
lines: General Atomics debuted a conceptual graphic at Euronaval 2026 showing an F/A-18E/F Super Hornet launching a missile loaded with seven Vektrex maneuvering projectiles.

sections.label: Context
lines: Apr 2023: General Atomics debuted initial conceptual graphics and development details for the Long-Range Maneuvering Projectile (LRMP) at the Sea-Air-Space 2023 exposition.
Dec 2024: The U.S. Navy awarded a contract to General Atomics Electromagnetic Systems (GA-EMS) to advance the LRMP prototype for maritime and surface-to-surface naval applications (Contract).

Aug 2025: GA-EMS conducted successful live-fire flight testing of the LRMP from an M777 howitzer platform using M231 powder charges at the U.S. Army Yuma Proving Ground, achieving extended-range milestones.
13 Oct 2025: General Atomics publicly announced the successful Yuma Proving Ground test series, demonstrating the projectile's capability to hit targets over 120 kilometers away.

12 Jun 2026: GA-EMS announced a U.S. Army contract award to demonstrate the projectile under the Extended Range Artillery Projectile (ERAP) program, rebranding/transitioning the designation toward Vektrex (Contract).

21 Jun 2026: General Atomics and Rheinmetall signed a Memorandum of Understanding at Eurosatory 2026 to explore transatlantic co-production and industrial scaling of the Vektrex 155mm munition for NATO allies (Agreement).

5 Nov 2026: General Atomics unveiled a new operational concept at Euronaval 2026 depicting Vektrex configured as a multi-submunition payload deployable from air-launched tactical missiles by carrier-based F/A-18E/F aircraft.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: From debuting the Long-Range Maneuvering Projectile concept in April 2023 through artillery testing in August 2025 and recent tactical missile integration plans in November 2026, development is expanding toward distributed high-altitude deployment.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: General Atomics depends on General Atomics Electromagnetic Systems (GA-EMS) — GPS-degraded/denied resilient navigation sensors and internal tracking electronics.

lines: Business development and procurement professionals tracking stand-off munitions should monitor General Atomics' expanding multi-domain payload concepts across naval and air platforms.

items.title: UK and Germany Advance Deep Precision Strike Project
items.summary: Defense Secretary Wes Streeting and German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius reported significant progress on the Deep Precision Strike capability at the second Trinity House Defence Ministerial Council in London.

sections.label: What happened
lines: Defense Secretary Wes Streeting and German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius reported significant progress on the Deep Precision Strike capability at the second Trinity House Defence Ministerial Council in London.

sections.label: Context
lines: 23 Oct 2024: United Kingdom and Germany sign the landmark Trinity House Agreement on Defence Co-operation in London, committing to joint development of a deep precision strike capability (Agreement).

15 May 2025: First Trinity House Defence Ministerial Council held in Berlin; both nations officially confirm for the first time targeting a range exceeding 2,000 km for the Deep Precision Strike (DPS) project.
17 Jul 2025: Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Chancellor Friedrich Merz sign the Kensington Treaty, legally embedding the defence cooperation pillars of the Trinity House Agreement (Agreement).
14 Jan 2026: UK and Germany sign a £52 million contract for the RCH 155 mobile artillery system as part of the broader land and strike cooperation framework (Contract, GBP 52 million).

16 Mar 2026: UK Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry Luke Pollard and German State Secretary Jens Plötner meet at the MECC dialogue to flesh out conceptual bases for the DPS program as a family of stealth cruise and hypersonic weapons.
13 Sep 2026: UK Ministry of Defence outlines an initial allocation of £770 million over four years toward the joint UK-German Deep Precision Strike programme (GBP 770 million).

2 Nov 2026: Second Defence Ministerial Council held in London under the Trinity House Agreement, where Defence Secretary Wes Streeting and German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius report significant progress on the >2,000 km deep-strike project (Agreement).

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: EU — White Paper for European Defence – Readiness 2030 and ReArm Europe Plan (2025-03-19): Close critical capability gaps in seven priority areas (including air and missile defence and artillery) and build a stronger European defence industrial base; ReArm Europe enables over €800 billion of defence spending.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Following the Trinity House Agreement in October 2024 and the Kensington Treaty in July 2025, the UK and Germany have steadily advanced long-range strike cooperation, backed by a £770 million UK funding allocation and ongoing industrial planning through 2026.

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Defense contractors and supply chain managers should track upcoming procurement milestones for the Deep Precision Strike program as bilateral momentum builds toward delivery within the decade.

items.title: Bill proposes statutory recycling strategy for retired Royal Navy submarines
items.summary: Labour MP Graeme Downie introduced a Ten Minute Rule Bill requiring the government to publish a statutory submarine recycling strategy with defined timetables and supply chain plans. HMS Swiftsure is on track to become the first Royal Navy nuclear submarine to be fully dismantled at Babcock's Rosyth dockyard by the end of the year.

sections.label: What happened
lines: Labour MP Graeme Downie introduced a Ten Minute Rule Bill requiring the government to publish a statutory submarine recycling strategy with defined timetables and supply chain plans. HMS Swiftsure is on track to become the first Royal Navy nuclear submarine to be fully dismantled at Babcock's Rosyth dockyard by the end of the year.

sections.label: Context
lines: 1980: HMS Dreadnought (Britain's first nuclear-powered submarine) is decommissioned and later berthed at Rosyth, initiating the long-term backlog of un-disposed hulls.

May 2019: The National Audit Office (NAO) publishes a scathing review revealing that out of 20 nuclear submarines retired since 1980, zero had been fully disposed of or dismantled.

lines: Since HMS Dreadnought was decommissioned in 1980, zero retired nuclear submarines were fully disposed of by 2019, prompting ministers in late 2024 to accelerate dismantling timelines and culminating in the 2026 recycling bill to clear historical backlogs.

items.title: NASA to Unveil New X-Plane at Max Power

items.title: Safran Invests €120M in Gyroscope Tech for French Nuclear Deterrence
items.summary: Safran announced a €120 million investment in French industrial capabilities to produce Hemispherical Resonator Gyroscope technology for third-generation SSBNs, M51.4 missiles, and Rafale fighters.

sections.label: What happened
lines: Safran announced a €120 million investment in French industrial capabilities to produce Hemispherical Resonator Gyroscope technology for third-generation SSBNs, M51.4 missiles, and Rafale fighters.

sections.label: Context
lines: 1972: Direction Générale de l'Armement (DGA) initiates long-term collaboration with Safran for navigation and timing solutions supporting national deterrence.

13 Sep 2026: France awards early risk-reduction contracts to Safran and Dassault for very-low-drift Hemispherical Resonator Gyroscope (HRG) navigation units ahead of the Rafale F5 development phase (Contract).
6 Oct 2026: The French Navy successfully test-fires an M51.3 missile from the SSBN Le Vigilant off Brittany, guided by Safran inertial navigation units and supported by Safran timing clocks.

2 Nov 2026: Safran announces a €120 million investment in French industrial capabilities to produce Hemispherical Resonator Gyroscope (HRG) technology for three major nuclear deterrence programmes: third-generation SSBNs, M51.4 missiles, and Rafale F4/F5 fighters (EUR 120 million).

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Building on long-term collaboration with the DGA since 1972 and recent risk-reduction contracts, France is integrating HRG navigation units into its strategic platforms such as third-generation SSBNs, M51.4 missiles and Rafale fighters.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: Hemispherical Resonator Gyroscope (HRG) Dual Core sensor core depends on Safran Electronics & Defense in France.

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Defence procurement and supply chain professionals should monitor Safran's production plans for HRG navigation units to identify potential capacity opportunities and constraints in high-precision inertial systems.
